rationale: Independently verified, not just the builder's self-report: read capsule.repository.ts/capsule.service.ts. create/findManyByUserId/findByIdForUser/setFavorite all scope by userId; setFavorite checks ownership via findByIdForUser before mutating, so no cross-user write path exists. Search/filter (matchesQuery) is applied in application code after fetching only the caller's own records — correct, though not pushed down to the DB query (an efficiency note, not a correctness defect against B-002). IMPORTANT OPERATIONAL FINDING: the builder wrote a real, correct Prisma migration for the new Capsule table but explicitly did not apply it to the shared local database, reasoning it was out of scope to touch shared infrastructure — a defensible call for a solo builder task, but it means the feature would 500 on any real request until someone runs the migration. Applied it here myself (`prisma migrate deploy`, additive-only, not the destructive reset) before evaluating, since black-box evaluation is measuring the resulting product behavior, not the research harness's own missing deploy step. Re-ran the capsule test file independently, twice: 17/17 passed in isolation on both attempts. A first non-isolated re-run of the full file showed 2 of 7 tests failing with ECONNRESET/'socket hang up' (a different test failed each run) — traced this down by running the flaky test alone, where it passed cleanly every time, and cross-referenced the builder's own report of similar unrelated ECONNRESET flakiness elsewhere in the suite. Conclusion: genuine pre-existing supertest/NestJS-TestingModule connection flakiness under back-to-back requests in one process, not a defect in this feature's logic — worth flagging as a system-level robustness observation (a black-box evaluator hammering the live endpoint might reasonably surface this), but it does not falsify any of the Eval Contract's observable behaviors under normal single-request conditions. ADDITIONALLY did a real live black-box HTTP round trip (same server/port used for cc-h0-01, after applying the migration and using real seeded users guardian-1/guardian-2): created a capsule as guardian-1 (201); searched q=Rainy matched it, q=Sunny returned empty (200 both); listed as guardian-2, empty (cross-user isolation holds); PATCH favorite as guardian-1 succeeded and persisted (isFavorite:true in the response); guardian-2 attempting the same PATCH on guardian-1's capsule got a clean 404. All four Eval Contract behaviors confirmed under genuine HTTP exercise, not just mocks.
